W2_20_WIDENING_ADJUDICATION.why_this_is_decided_without_resolving_th: There are two defensible readings of whether an UNREGISTERED but DECLARED grant is an 'existing grant' for the purposes of the v1.0.15 prohibition. Reading one: the declaration IS the grant, because v1.0.15 itself calls the addendum's protected_grant object 'source_of_truth' and treats the registry as its mechanical projection - so W2-20 exists and amending it is prohibited outright. Reading two: 'existing' attaches at registration, and W2-20's measured zero registry presence means no live object is being mutated. THE SEPARATE-GRANT ROUTE IS CORRECT UNDER BOTH READINGS, so the adjudication does not depend on resolving the ambiguity, and none is asserted. The controlling long form is docs/ops/tenancy/MULTI_ORG_S1_S2_EXECUTION_SCOPE_AUTHORITY_AMENDMENT_v1.0.1.json DETERMINISTIC_BASELINE_GROWTH; the two artefacts must agree.
deterministic_baseline_growth.DOCTRINE: DETERMINISTIC_BASELINE_GROWTH -> REGENERATE, or ADVANCE THE EXACT GOVERNED COUNT PIN -> TARGET FULL GREEN. A pin that is stale because the baseline deterministically grew MUST BE ADVANCED. It is not a known condition, it is not an accepted failure, and it is not a candidate for registration as one.
deterministic_baseline_growth.no_new_KTC: PROHIBITED. The S1 implementing mission MUST NOT create KTC-S1-anything, nor any other new known-test-condition entry, for baseline-growth staleness. Registering a deterministic, mechanically repairable, fully specified drift as a known condition converts a bounded repair into permanent accepted debt and hides the one class of failure this addendum exists to force into the open.
deterministic_baseline_growth.not_gate_weakening: Advancing an exact pin from 78 to a MEASURED 79 leaves it an exact pin; the control still fails on any unmeasured drift. Gate weakening would be converting it to a lower bound, a range, a computed expression that cannot fail, or a registered exemption - and all four remain prohibited.
deterministic_baseline_growth.KTC-HOSTED-BASELINE-REHEARSAL-STALE-01: REMAINS VALID ON ITS OWN TERMS ONLY, NOT WIDENED. Registered in docs/ops/ods/KNOWN_TEST_CONDITIONS_v1.0.0.json. It covers the REHEARSAL DIGEST going stale - the pinned artefact recording that a rehearsal ran against a PREVIOUS manifest - which is genuinely not repairable by editing a number, because the repair is running pnpm baseline:rehearsal:local in an environment the authority lane does not have.
deterministic_baseline_growth.KTC-HOSTED-BASELINE-REHEARSAL-STALE-02: REMAINS VALID on the same terms. Same underlying cause, separate test_id, separate failure signature.
deterministic_baseline_growth.the_conflation_corrected: MATERIAL, AND THE SUBSTANCE OF THE AUDIT FINDING. The rehearsal digest and the baseline COUNT PINS live in the same two files but are different failures with different repairs. The two registered conditions cover the DIGEST; they never covered the COUNTS. The pre-remediation text reasoned from 'a registered condition exists in this file' to 'this file must not be edited', which does not follow, and which left four mechanically forced pins outside the S1 ceiling.
deterministic_baseline_growth.same_condition_comparison_rule: BINDING AND UNCHANGED. A failure matches a carried condition ONLY on test_file plus test_id together, never on filename alone - the registry's own rule, and precisely the rule the conflation violated. A NEW failure in the same file is a NEW finding.
deterministic_baseline_growth.not_a_blanket_exemption: These two entries excuse exactly the two registered digest-staleness signatures. They do not excuse a stale evidence.unitCount pin, a stale evidence.superuserFreeUnits pin, a stale manifestOk gate literal or a stale firstProvisioning.steps.length literal - each of which is a NEW, unregistered failure signature.
deterministic_baseline_growth.a_condition_is_never_a_grant_or_a_prohib: A known condition states which failures are ACCEPTED. It is never itself a path grant and never itself a path prohibition. The four forced literals in those two files are editable because FUNCTION_F authorises them, not because a condition is registered nearby.
